chapter: Sue and Patsy Howard in show business
title: Working with the Ellington band in Jump for Joy
summary: Patsy remembers the band as fantastic and rehearsals as joyful, naming Ray Nance, Jimmy Blanton and Ben Webster.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: How about the Ellington band?
Oh, just fantastic.
Was that the first time you met them, or had you met them before?
No, I had known them but I had never worked with them. Like I'd known Duke and Barney Bigard and Sonny --
Greer?
Greer. And -- oh, I knew quite a few of them.
They had played the Cotton Club.
Well, I wasn't --
They didn't play there.
Did they play the Cotton Club here?
Who?
Duke. No.
They didn't, no.
Only in New York, yeah. A fantastic orchestra.
Sure were.
Just beautiful. And Duke was a beautiful person to work with.
Can you remember any of the things that happened there, any of the things that might not be written down somewhere?

Well, no, not exactly, because everyone got along so well, and rehearsals were beautiful, it wasn't one of those that was tiresome or -- everybody enjoyed even rehearsing. It was really beautiful. And it had a choir and --
Did -- Ray Nante was in the band then.
Yeah, Ray Nante was in the band.
Did he ever dance then, or did his dancing start later?
I don't know. He didn't dance in that show.
Because later on he would dance with the band.
Yeah, well-- and playing his violin and everything.
Whatever he felt like doing.
Yeah, right.
(Inaudible) and Jimmy Blanton was there.
Yeah, Jimmy Blanton.
And Ben Webster.
Yeah, Ben Webster, they were all there. It was a fantastic band.
